reason: E1 directly demonstrates that cryo-rolling and annealing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA produces a refined hierarchical microstructure with YS ~1437 MPa and elongation ~14%, supporting all key premises. E3 and E8 explain the back-stress strengthening mechanism in such heterogeneous structures. E6 provides evidence that strong phase boundaries reduce dislocation pile-ups and crack nucleation. The cited evidence accurately represents the proposed mechanism and outcomes, with no contradictions.
premises: Cryo-rolling followed by annealing refines the hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The refined microstructure reduces dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries, mitigating local stress concentrations.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups overcomes brittleness and improves ductility.
The heterogeneous microstructure promotes back-stress strengthening, retaining or increasing strength.
The treatment yields simultaneous improvement in strength (~1400 MPa YS) and ductility (~14% elongation) over the as-cast state.
